transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-23
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Alicia Chen (Redwood AE), Marco Ruiz (Redwood SE), Jared Lowe (CTO, Sable), Priya Nair (Lead ML Eng, Sable), Tom Becker (Infra Manager, Sable)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, optional):
Sable Ventures is evaluating hosting options for an LLM-powered pilot: hosted Redwood API vs Dedicated reserved capacity vs Private VPC deployment. Primary success criteria: 95th-percentile latency under 400ms for 512-token interactions, cost under $X per 1M tokens (TBD), and SOC 2 + KMS compliance. Action items include sharing security docs, providing traffic profile, and scheduling benchmark runs.

Topics:
- Success criteria and SLAs
- Workload sizing (QPS, token distribution, seq length)
- Benchmark plan (metrics and scripts)
- Timeline and pilot scope
- Security and data residency requirements

Action items (brief): see metadata list above.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Alicia Chen: okay hey everyone, thanks for joining, um we wanted to run through Sable's pilot scope and, uh, make sure we align on the metrics that matter and the hosting decision tradeoffs. Marco and I will cover technical bits, and then we'll map next steps.
[00:23] Jared Lowe: thanks, Alicia. quick bit of context — we're looking to add a conversational summarization feature inside our dealflow portal, so latency matters and we have some PII concerns. timeline is Q3 pilot, production by Q4 if things go well.
[00:45] Priya Nair: yeah and on perf im mainly worried about p95 latency under 400 millis at typical load and we'd like to keep cost predictable; we have some line items about dedicated capacity for month-to-month predictability.
[01:05] Marco Ruiz: cool. to frame it: Redwood offers hosted API for fastest time-to-value, Dedicated for reserved GPU pools, and Private for VPC/on-prem where you need enclave-like control. for benchmarks we usually measure latency p50/p95, tokens/sec, and token cost.
[01:32] Tom Becker: when you say private, are we talking fully customer-managed hardware or a customer VPC in your control plane? we have some compliance folks who want the network off the public internet.
[01:45] Marco Ruiz: good question — private deployment can be two flavors. one is Redwood Private in a customer VPC with our control plane optionally in their region; the other is on-prem packaged deploy where you run the control plane locally. both support KMS integrations and audit logs.
[02:10] Jared Lowe: ok. so can you summarize the tradeoffs quickly? like latencies, cost, ops overhead?
[02:18] Alicia Chen: absolutely. hosted is lowest ops and fastest rollout — you hit our hosted API and we manage autoscaling; latency good for many workloads but shared tenancy means slightly higher tail variability. Dedicated gives you predictable throughput and lower variance, better cost per token for committed usage. Private gives max isolation and compliance but higher ops and longer lead time.
[02:45] Priya Nair: for our use case we have spikes tied to daily digest runs plus interactive agents. spikes can 3x baseline. our baseline is 10 qps with 2K tokens/session peak, interactive is 30 qps but shorter 512 token completions.
[03:06] Marco Ruiz: helpful — so our pilot should test both steady-state and spike loads. we'll recommend two benchmark profiles: 1) interactive micro: 512-token completions, 30 qps sustained for 5 minutes, measure p95/throughput; 2) bulk digest: 2k token sequences at 10 qps for 10 minutes and KV cache warm/cold cases.
[03:35] Jared Lowe: and what about batch sizes and quantization? we might accept a little quality drop if cost improves.
[03:42] Marco Ruiz: we can try int8 and int4 quantization profiles. Redwood Optimize will suggest quantization versus quality tradeoffs; for the pilot we typically run baseline float32 or bf16 when evaluating latency and then run quantized variants to measure cost delta.
[04:05] Priya Nair: can you give a ballpark cost per million tokens for hosted vs dedicated? i know it's fuzzy.
[04:12] Alicia Chen: ballpark numbers: hosted tends to be higher per-token on bursts, so maybe 30-50% above dedicated at scale. dedicated committed can be 40-60% cheaper than hosted once you hit the commit threshold. private depends heavily on your infra costs; often similar to dedicated but with ops overhead. we'll put exact pilot pricing in the SOW.
[04:39] Tom Becker: sounds fair. security: we need SOC2 Type II, SAML SSO, RBAC, customer-managed keys. can you confirm those are supported in dedicated and private?
[04:51] Marco Ruiz: yes — Dedicated and Private both support SSO via SAML, RBAC, and KMS/HSM integration for key management. hosted API supports encryption in transit and at rest and can integrate with an external KMS for enterprise customers under a private contract — details we'll include in the security packet.
[05:15] Jared Lowe: great. let's talk success criteria. beyond p95 < 400ms for interactive, we want accurate NPS-style quality metric: less than 5% hallucination on our eval set. also cost per 1M tokens under a threshold, and smooth autoscaling during digest job spikes.
[05:35] Alicia Chen: perfect. so pilot success criteria we propose: (1) interactive p95 < 400ms for 512-token payloads, (2) hallucination <= 5% on your eval set using our eval harness, (3) cost delta target (we'll quantify) and (4) SSO + KMS validated. are we missing anything?
[05:58] Priya Nair: also need throughput stability — during 3x spikes we can't have cold-start penalties causing cascading queueing.
[06:06] Marco Ruiz: we'll include warm cache and cold cache runs. Redwood's KV cache and prefix caching will be explicitly tested — we instrument token-level latency and cache hit ratios.
[06:20] Jared Lowe: timeline then — we want a short pilot to decide by end of Q3. is a 6-week pilot reasonable?
[06:28] Alicia Chen: yes 6 weeks aligns with our typical pilot: week 0 on boarding and infra, weeks 1-3 benchmarks and iteration, weeks 4-5 quantization and regression tests, week 6 wrap and exec review.
[06:44] Tom Becker: what infra prep do you need from our side for Dedicated vs Private?
[06:49] Marco Ruiz: Dedicated — we need firewall rules, egress allowances to Redwood endpoints, and a test service account. for Private — we'll need VPC peering details, subnets, and if on-prem, a list of hosts plus network ACLs. we'll send a checklist.
[07:06] Priya Nair: if we do hosted first to move fast, could we later migrate to Dedicated or Private without rewriting the app?
[07:14] Marco Ruiz: yes that's a key Redwood premise: same API surface and rollout files. you can pin model versions and switch routing policies. migration typically requires config changes and re-tuning batching, but no code rewrite.
[07:28] Jared Lowe: okay great. can you run me through a sample benchmark metric set and what we should expect in the report?
[07:37] Marco Ruiz: we'll report p50/p95/p99 latencies, tokens/sec, total compute used (GPU-hours), cache hit ratios, cost per 1M tokens estimate, and quality metrics on your eval set (bleu/f1/ROUGE-like or our custom hallucination score). we'll also show traces for tail latency events.
[08:05] Priya Nair: slight tangent — does Redwood support dynamic batching for variable-length sequences? we have very spiky seq lengths.
[08:15] Marco Ruiz: yes, runtime supports continuous batching with attention optimizations and dynamic padding; for very variable seq lengths we may recommend route-by-key to avoid worst-case padding. we'll capture delta in the benchmark.
[08:31] Jared Lowe: any known gotchas migrating models that use long-context attention? our digest uses 8k tokens sometimes.
[08:39] Marco Ruiz: long context is supported but affects kernel selection and memory. for 8k contexts we typically recommend specific model variants plus quantization and possibly splitting pipelines for summarization. that'll be part of the dedicated/private sizing conversation.
[08:56] Priya Nair: for the pilot scripts, we can provide sample prompts and an eval set. what format do you want?
[09:02] Marco Ruiz: CSV with columns: prompt_id, prompt_text, expected_output_snippet, avg_seq_len, and a column for whether it includes sensitive PII. also a traffic profile CSV with timestamped qps or histogram.
[09:20] Alicia Chen: perfect. on next steps — we'll send SOW and the security packet; Marco will send benchmark scripts. we'll target the first benchmark run next Tuesday as discussed.
[09:33] Jared Lowe: okay. let's surface procurement timeline — we'll likely need an MSA signed before Dedicated or Private. is that standard?
[09:40] Alicia Chen: yes we have a standard MSA and addendum for private deployments; for hosted pilots we can often start with a pilot agreement that short-circuits the full MSA depending on risk profile.
[09:52] Tom Becker: question: are there any limits on model size for Dedicated? we want a 70B model for quality.
[09:58] Marco Ruiz: Dedicated supports up to 70B generally depending on GPU flavor and memory; if you need 70B with long context and high qps, we may recommend distribution across multiple GPUs or a model shard config. we'll size that in the pilot.
[10:15] Priya Nair: can we run a small smoke test today against hosted so we can sanity check prompts?
[10:20] Alicia Chen: yes we can spin a temporary test key and run a handful of prompt tests. Marco, can you follow up?
[10:25] Marco Ruiz: yep i'll send a quickstart notebook and an example test harness with instructions after the call.
[10:30] Jared Lowe: good. any competitors we should be aware of for cost comparisons?
[10:34] Tom Becker: we've chatted with CloudAI Services and AtlasInference; they both pitched reserved endpoints.
[10:39] Marco Ruiz: noted — we'll include a competitive note in the SOW outlining where Redwood typically wins (throughput/cost controls and unified API) and where tradeoffs exist.
[10:52] Priya Nair: ok quick clarification on benchmarks — do you simulate cold starts? we want to see tail blips during spike ramp-ups.
[10:58] Marco Ruiz: yes we simulate ramp-ups at multiple speeds and record cold-to-warm transitions. we'll also test cache eviction scenarios.
[11:10] Jared Lowe: can you include a simple dashboard sample so our PMs can follow along?
[11:15] Alicia Chen: yes Redwood Console screenshots and a sample dashboard export will be in the packet.
[11:24] Tom Becker: last question, for Private on-prem, what is typical lead time for onboarding?
[11:29] Marco Ruiz: Private on-prem usually takes 4-8 weeks depending on network and security reviews; VPC-hosted private is often 2-4 weeks. Dedicated can be faster if capacity is available.
[11:45] Priya Nair: that might push our Q3 timeline if we pick Private. maybe we start hosted then flip to Dedicated in prod.
[11:51] Alicia Chen: many customers do that exact path. we'll document migration steps.
[12:03] Jared Lowe: alright i think that's a wrap. thanks everyone.
[12:07] Alicia Chen: thanks, we'll follow up with SOW and pilot materials.

(Transcript ends)
